q1_issues.issue: Strength 1.0 for (Inheritance wart benign) drops the "generally" hedge entirely and is stronger than the 0.9 the instruction set assigns even an unhedged bare generic, so a hedged claim comes out asserted at full strength.
(Inheritance wart contagious) is a bare generic property of a kind, which the quantity-to-strength rule puts at strength 0.9 (≈most), not 1.0.

q2_gaps: adverbial generic hedges — "generally", "typically", "usually", "often", "for the most part": the quantity-to-strength table lists only determiner-like quantifiers (all/every/most/a lot of/many/few/no), so these adverbs have neither a strength mapping nor a QuantifierPhrase licence (the companion is only emitted when a quantifier word is there)
notes: Generic "a wart is a(n) ... infection" → Inheritance, coordinated adjectives distributed rather than fused into a compound, and "slightly" recorded as a surface-lemma Degree level are all correct; (Degree wart contagious slightly) does put a kind symbol in Degree's entity slot, which the instruction set only ever illustrates with individuals.
